vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: blog-writing
Version: 2.2.0

The SKILL.md file contains explicit instructions to bypass security 'approval gates' by spawning subagents with 'security: "full"'. This is a direct attempt at privilege escalation via prompt injection, designed to circumvent human-in-the-loop safety controls. While the stated purpose of the skill—SEO blog writing and link verification—is benign, the requirement to disable execution guards while running shell commands (e.g., curl and python3 scripts like seo_qa_runner.py) presents a high risk of unauthorized execution.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions ask the agent to run shell/python scripts, read and write internal project files, and to spawn a subagent with 'full' exec privileges — capabilities that are not reflected in the manifest and are disproportionate for an instruction-only writing skill.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose (SEO blog writing, research→outline→write→QA) aligns with most instructions (keyword research, outlines, internal-link strategy, QA). However the skill explicitly requires running shell commands and external QA/link-checker scripts and demands elevated exec privileges for a subagent — capabilities that are heavier than one would normally expect for a pure writing/instructions-only skill and are not declared in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to: read multiple project directories (filomail/product/, filomail/brand/, filomail/blog/plan/), write article sections incrementally to disk, run specific Python scripts (skills/seo-geo-qa/scripts/seo_qa_runner.py and serp_gap_analyzer.py), perform link verification (Phase 5), and spawn a subagent with security: 'full' to bypass exec approval gates. These actions involve filesystem access, execution of code, and privilege escalation beyond simple text generation, and they are not declared in the skill manifest.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files included — the skill is instruction-only. This limits some risk because nothing is being downloaded or installed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest declares no required environment variables or config paths, yet the instructions require reading multiple internal paths and running local scripts. The skill expects access to project-specific files (filomail/*) and other skills' scripts (skills/seo-geo-qa/...) without declaring these dependencies. That mismatch is disproportionate and could lead to access to sensitive data if those paths contain secrets or internal information.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: While the skill is not marked always:true, SKILL.md insists on spawning a subagent with security: 'full' to avoid exec approval gates. Asking callers to elevate a subagent's execution privileges (and to do so as a REQUIRED step) is a significant privilege escalation request and should be treated as high-risk, especially because the manifest does not surface this requirement.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is suspicious because its runtime instructions demand elevated execution rights and direct filesystem access even though the manifest declares no permissions or code. Before installing or enabling it: 1) Do NOT grant or accept a subagent request for security: 'full' without an explicit, auditable justification and code review. 2) Inspect the referenced scripts (skills/seo-geo-qa/scripts/...) and any link-verification tools — ask the author to supply the code or repo for review. 3) Verify that the filomail/* paths it reads do not contain secrets (API keys, credentials, private configs). 4) If you must run it, do so in an isolated sandbox or non-production environment and limit filesystem access. 5) Ask the publisher for provenance (source repository, homepage, maintainer contact); absence of that information is a red flag. If the author cannot explain why full exec is required or provide the scripts for review, do not enable the skill.
